Job Description:
ROLE DESCRIPTION:
SAP's Global Communications unit is charged with protecting and enhancing the reputation of SAP with internal and external audiences. To that end, GC strives to position SAP as the world’s leading business cloud software solution provider, recognized thought leader, responsible corporate citizen, as well as employer, business partner, vendor, and investment of choice. In addition, the communications function supports sales of SAP software solutions and products, informs employees about strategy, performance and execution and drives employee engagement.
GC programs are geared towards influencing SAP’s primary audiences - customers, employees, government officials, and partners either indirectly via influencers such as Media (print, online, broadcast), Bloggers, Industry Analysts, or directly as in the case of our communication with employees, managers and government representatives. “Customers” of SAP’s communications function are therefore both the internal stakeholders representing SAP’s business, our employees, and the relevant external influencers.
In that context, the Integrated Communications functions within GC are responsible for planning and driving the execution of communications activities across these multiple audiences. Integrated communications functions within GC exist on the global, regional, and local levels.
EXPECTATIONS AND TASKS:
The Senior Specialist in this function leads the local communications team and is Is part of a virtual regional team spanning EMEA South.
The Senior Specialist level of Integrated Communications covers all or an agreed selection of GC’s communications programs and channels for the assigned market unit (Africa) and may be requested to participate or lead special projects within GC community.
The Senior Specialist represents the communications function on the Africa Senior Leadership team and may be requested to lead or participate in cross-Africa initiatives that support the business priorities or employee experience.
At the Senior Specialist level this job includes hands-on media relations, employee communications, full executive communications for the SAP Africa Managing Director (developing and sharing content, shaping channels, and reaching out to audiences), a lighter version of executive communications for the Executive Leadership team, as well as working closely with team members to support cross-regional and corporate activities and topics, including those related to SAP’s Corporate Social Responsibility and other global and local initiatives.
The Senior Specialist must be able to manage complex crises across numerous stakeholders at local, regional and global level – orchestrating proactive and reactive plans to manage crises and reputation challenges.
Full time role FTE, based in Johannesburg, South Africa.
Major Responsibilities include:
Provide communications counsel to SAP Africa Managing Director, country leadership and the employees of the market unit.
Create thought leadership awareness in the media and ensure the global and regional priorities are adhered to deliver a strong rolling volume of media coverage and message penetration.
Ensure crises are managed, coordinated and escalated to region and GC leaders where necessary, in collaboration with other functions and agencies.
Build and strengthen a network of regional/national media contacts and media categories (online, print, social media, broadcast, business, trade and verticals)
Support in developing a news pipeline that strengthens SAP’s public profile with regard to business strategy, innovation, customer stories and thought leadership as well as leading market position in business software.
Engage and manage selected external media agency, providing clear direction and focus to ensure alignment to global and local messages and ensure message and media training for industry and product spokespeople.
Develop a communications plan in support of the Africa and regional GTM strategies and provide regular updates to progress against plan goals as well as defining and managing budget requirements.
Drive regular communication channels and work with various teams to provide content for regular company updates or Town Hall meetings, ownership of the local Customer Success Sales kick-off content.
Manage internal communications that focuses on consistent and engaging messaging for employees – working strongly with HR and local business leaders based on the company business plan and company vision to create consistent key messages.
WORK EXPERIENCE:
10+ years relevant working experience
Experience in Senior Management positions.
Ability to perform duties of Senior Company Spokesperson with range of communications stakeholders.
Knowledge of the SAP Product portfolio advantageous
Experience in design and implementation of communications concepts and plans.
Experience in communications to more than one influencer type (media, bloggers, analyst, governments officials, employee communications).
Experience in story-telling and copy-writing / briefing framework for copy-writing to incumbent external agency.
Experienced in handling confidential material.
Experience in providing communications counsel to senior local and global executives.

English is either your native language or you have excellent English writing and editing skills.
University Degree desired (or equivalent education).
Professional communicator.
Self-motivated and team oriented.
Exceptional project management skills.
Ability to navigate ambiguity and adapt to change.
Strong creative approach to conceptualise, design and implement new programmes to reach changing media landscape.
Flexible and able to cope with stress.
Understanding of IT market in Africa including Southern, West and East Africa.
Ability to translate corporate strategy into powerful messages for various communications disciplines.

Ensure productivity levels are optimised.

Job Description:
Description – Robotics Engineer
A highly motivated robotics engineer or controls engineer with a strong track record in robotics and machine automation to contribute to and be part of a team whose main objective will be to design and develop new, and refine existing systems, for automation in oil and gas drill floor activities, with the primary emphasis being improved safety, efficiency, and robust execution of handling operations.
This role will be a technically challenging one in a dynamic environment. The role will present the successful candidate with opportunities to contribute to the continued success of NOV, a company with an unmatched pedigree and a huge legacy of innovation and technological advancement in the Oil and Gas Industry.
Duties & Responsibilities
Review existing drill floor equipment with a view to redesigning for use in hands-free and/or automated pipe handling and drilling.
Conduct research on robotic hardware and software technologies to create new robotic systems or system capabilities.
Conduct research into effective, optimized path planning with advanced collision detection and/collision avoidance algorithms.
Participate in initial equipment conceptual ideas and development, specifications, and control requirements, for hands free and automated pipe handling and drilling, such as mobile omni-directional robots.
Research, assess, and where necessary design software and hardware systems for electromechanical equipment or systems, and advanced displays, advanced sensing, robotic platforms, computer vision.
Research, assess, and where necessary design software and hardware systems for robotic applications related to the drilling industry pipe-handling activities using robotic platforms, open source or commercial.
Introduce automated equipment and processes into oil and gas pipe handling and drilling, training aftermarket personnel to support after deployment.
Qualifications
Bachelors Degree in a related engineering field with practical experience in robotics and/or industrial automation, and 5 additional years of proven experience in the development of machine and automation controls
2 years of experience in designing and implementing machine controls systems, using PLC or embedded controllers
Working knowledge and experience of PLC and high level programming languages such as Java, C, C++, LabView, Siemens, and operating systems such as Linux
Ability to read P&ID, electrical and hydraulics schematics and translate into software environments.
Working knowledge of robotics platforms and tool kits both vendor specific (such as ABB, Yaskawa, Kawasaki, Kuka, etc) and vendor independent (such as ROS and ROS Industrial).
Preferred Qualifications / Skills
Knowledge of Oil and Gas drilling rig processes
Experience and working knowledge of AC drive systems
Experience of hydraulic systems and servo control
Experience and working knowledge of programing HMI systems
Working knowledge of machine vision systems and platforms
Understanding of AI systems and platforms

Job Description About the role
The Head of PMM for AMEAA is a leadership role that is accountable for the delivery of all PMM jobs and outputs within the region, as measured by the delivery of £150m+ ARR and 10%+ annual growth. This role leads the virtual AMEAA PMM Squad to deliver these specific outcomes:
Deeply understand the needs of customers, the trends/dynamics in the market and competitors – and ensuring this is injected into Business Units so they build winning Strategies and Growth Plans.
Build, and regularly update, an AMEAA Growth Plan and Launch Calendar that defines the market opportunity, as well as timing and execution of the Growth Initiatives needed to achieve the regional Growth Targets.
Support the creation, regular updating/re-planning and execution of an achievable AMEAA Win Plan that meets or exceeds the Growth Targets.
Ensures that all AMEAA Growth Initiatives and PMM deliverables are properly planned, strongly executed and then refined post-execution to deliver the expected commercial results. And the jobs to be done/outputs produced follow the PMM Ways of Working.
Becomes the trusted PMM business partner to AMEAA Managing Director/Leadership Teams, acting as the single point of contact for all PMM and Business Unit deliverables for the Region, leads effective and efficient alignment; and proactively solving risks/issues.
The Head of PMM for AMEAA delivers these outcomes through leadership of the virtual AMEAA PMM Squad across the BUs. They’re accountable for ensuring the squad has the right culture, resourcing, capabilities, objectives/goals and influence into their BUs to achieve the required outcomes for the AMEAA. They also ensure that all jobs to be done and outputs produced within the Region follow the PMM Ways of Working. And, as senior leaders within PMM, they are also accountable for providing local PMM leadership to colleagues based in their region with ongoing coaching, talent development and recruitment.
Success in this role is measured by the achievement of Region ARR and Growth Targets, as well as the effectiveness of the relationships with both Region MDs/Leadership Teams and Business Units. To achieve this, the Head of PMM AMEAA requires strong leadership skills working within and across a matrix organisation, specifically the ability to lead a virtual team of PMM Professionals to drive winning outcomes. Of equal importance is the need for strong persuasion, negotiation and communication skills, which are all critical to developing effective and trusted relationships with Region Managing Directors/Leadership Teams and Heads of PMM for BUs.
A key success factor will be establishing strong, trusted relationships with the MD and Senior Leadership Teams across the Regions; becoming integrated into these teams and developing the ability to robustly challenge on a peer to peer basis.
Key Responsibilities
Region PMM Squad Leadership – accountable for leading the (virtual) AMEAA PMM Squad to deliver the required PMM jobs and outputs for the region. Responsible for co-setting objectives and goals, driving the squad to achieve daily/weekly/monthly outcomes for the region and supporting BU Leaders in the coaching and development of squad members.
Region Interlock - acts as the primary point of contact for AMEAA MDs and LT into central PMM, by owning and resolving risks/issues and ensuring that the Region insight/voice/needs successfully flows into PMM Business Units.
Region Growth Plans - ensuring that Business Unit (BU) Growth Plans and GoToMarket programmes are successfully translated into robust, ambitious and realistic AMEAA Growth Plan that achieve both BU and AMEAA growth targets.
Region Win Plans – supports the creation, regular updating/re-planning and execution of an achievable AMEAA Win Plan that meets/exceeds Growth Targets.
Region Launch Calendar – accountable for building and maintaining the Region Launch Calendar (in perfect alignment with each BUs) to become the single source of truth for what BUs (product, proposition, campaign launches) will deliver into the Region.
Region GTM Execution - leads the planning, execution and coordination of all GoToMarket activities (as outlined in BU and AMEAA Growth Plans) to ensure strong execution of plans, drive continuous improvement and manage opportunities/risks.
PMM Ways Of Working – ensures a simple, repeatable PMM Way of Working (the common framework - jobs to be done, outputs, processes, templates, goal setting) across every Business Unit within the Region, especially in the execution of all PMM jobs and outputs.
PMM Resourcing – accountable for the resourcing plan across PMM for the Region, working with and influencing BUs to ensure an effective and efficient balance of capability for the Region.

Who we are
Established in 1940, we are a national development finance institution set up to promote economic growth and industrial development. We are owned by the South African government under the supervision of the Economic Development Department.

Our vision
We aim to be the primary source of co...read moremmercially sustainable industrial development and innovation to benefit both South Africa and the rest of Africa.

Our mission
Our mandate is to contribute to the creation of balanced, sustainable economic growth in South Africa and on the rest of the continent.

We promote entrepreneurship through the building of competitive industries and enterprises based on sound business principles.

Our values
Everything we do is directed by our values:

 Passion
 Partnership
 Professionalism

Our mandate
The Industrial Development Corporation of South Africa Limited (IDC) was established in 1940 by an Act of Parliament (Industrial Development Corporation Act, No. 22 of 1940) and is fully owned by the South African Government.

The IDC was mandated to develop domestic industrial capacity, specifically in manufactured goods, to mitigate the disruption of trade between Europe and South Africa during the Second World War.

We have contributed to the implementation of South Africa's industrial policy for more than 70 years and established, among others, the petro-chemicals and minerals beneficiation industries. We have stimulated large industrial projects in these industries - acknowledged today as the cornerstones of the country's manufacturing sector - and influenced the establishment of industries in fabricated metals, agriculture and clothing and textiles.

During the 1990s, our mandate was expanded to include investment in the rest of Africa. The Mozal aluminium smelter in Mozambique was the first such venture. We secured investors from around the globe to establish a major industrial enterprise in a country plagued by decades of civil war. The smelter illustrated the viability of large projects on a continent often shunned by investors. Currently, our investments in Africa include mining, agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications.

The IDC's funding is generated through income from loan and equity investments and exits from mature investments, as well as borrowings from commercial banks, development finance institutions (DFIs) and other lenders.

We align our priorities with government's policy direction and remain committed to developing the country's industrial capacity, as well as playing a major role in facilitating job creation through industrialisation.
Our industrial development role
As a key implementing agency of industrial policy, the IDC's activities currently centre on the National Development Plan (NDP), the New Growth Path (NGP) and the Industrial Policy Action Plan (IPAP). We identify sector development opportunities aligned with policy objectives and develop projects in partnership with stakeholders.

By developing industrial capacity the IDC achieves specific outcomes. The most important of these is to enable job creation through the companies we fund. In addition, IDC funding continues to promote regional development and integration, economic empowerment of communities and growing black industrialists. The IDC remains committed to promoting environmentally sustainable growth and increasing sectoral diversity to boost the local production of goods. The corporation also plays a critical role, directly and through its sefa subsidiary, in promoting entrepreneurial development and growing the SME sector.

While our funding activities focus mainly on the private sector, we work closely with different levels of government agencies and sector organisations to coordinate industry development. We also support government in other areas related to its development objectives, such as research and management of government funds allocated to achieving specific outcomes. We pro-actively develop and implement strategies in the rest of Africa to create and integrate value chains across the continent. Our aim is to use the strengths of different countries in the region to establish a more competitive industrial base.

Job Title: Consultancy - Online Safety Programme: Capacity development of law enforcement and front-line workers, Pretoria, South Africa, 6 months
Job Description:
PURPOSE OF ACTIVITY/ASSIGNMENT:
Under the supervision of the Child Protection Specialist, the consultant will review/adapt and develop a training package content relevant to online violence prevention and safety measures for children using online platforms and will provide content to law enforcement agencies and frontline workers on their roles for prevention and risk mitigation including service delivery. The consultant is expected to review the literature and relevant documents including existing training materials, and then she/he will organize validation with government agencies. Develop a training roadmap and provide the training to front-line workers and law enforcement officials.
SCOPE OF WORK:
Background:
South Africa is a middle-income country more than 27 years into the advent of democracy with remarkable progress to improve the well-being of its citizens. South Africa is recognised for its strong legislative framework and policies, including implementing children’s rights as articulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child, The African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child, enshrined in the Constitution of SA and the Children’s Act. South Africa is faced with the triple challenges of enduring poverty, inequality and unemployment, which impact the lives of children. Almost two-thirds of the South African children live below the upper bound of the poverty line with children in rural areas and those living in female-headed households, particularly at risk.
The fast-developing and continuously changing information and communication technology (ICT) environment is reshaping children's lives globally. Now more than ever children are increasingly relying on online and mobile technologies to learn, participate, play, entertain and socialise. The digital age has brought opportunities to children and its use has been amplified by the Covid-19 pandemic. However, despite the many positive opportunities it provides, the internet also increases children's risk of abuse and exploitation and compounds offline risks and negative experiences such as bullying and harassment, exposure to pornographic and other potentially harmful materials, and possible dangerous contacts.
In 2021 UNICEF in partnership with the South Africa government conducted the National Kids Online Study as part of the Disrupting Harm Study to examine the opportunities and risks of ICT within a national context. The study revealed that most children (95.3%) and their parents/caregivers (80.2%) have access to the internet via a mobile device - which brings significant opportunities as well as risks. 70% of children use the internet without parental supervision and 1 in 3 children in South Africa are at risk of online exploitation. Risky online activities included meeting someone face-to-face with whom they met on the internet, actively seeking new friends, adding strangers as friends and sharing photos or videos of themselves with persons they have never met. Yet, many children remain silent about their experiences, with 50.5% of children not telling anyone what happened.
Scope of Work:
This consultancy reviews the package for capacity development material for the frontline workers and law enforcement agencies focusing on material developed in the previous phase. The package will be adopted in the South African context to ensure social and cultural sensitivity and relevance. The developed materials and toolkits will be aligned with the UNICEF global platforms of online safety, international instruments and national legislation and the network of ICT platforms available in SA. It will consider the law enforcement agencies and front-line workers who, support, work and educate children for prevention and response.
Activities and tasks:
Desk review: The consultant will conduct a literature review and pursue numerous online research documents, and training materials developed globally and in South Africa to produce relevant training packages for law enforcement and front-line workers.
Organize need-based joint consultation with relevant UNICEF section focal and government counterparts and non-governmental agencies within the National GBVF Collaborative addressing violence against women and children through the NSP on GBV implementation.
Conduct two focused interviews with stakeholders including government officials, and frontline workers that will support the development of training need assessment.
Develop the package of training materials and toolkits for the capacity development of law enforcement agencies and frontline workers. The consultant will cover materials for knowledge development on online safety issues including risk, prevention and mitigation strategies, the role of caregivers, and service providers, including appropriate content to promote the safety of children both online and offline. Take initiative for wider sharing with the Government counterparts, CSOs, and networks for final inputs on the content and training package.
Develop a roadmap for training delivery for law enforcement agencies and frontline workers within the timeframe.
Conduct training sessions with law enforcement agencies and front-line workers according to the training roadmaps.
Submit to UNICEF compiled reports to articulate the key progresses with challenges and the way forward for future implementation of the training package.

About Job
Sanofi Global Health aims to improve access to care for underserved patients in 40 high-need countries mainly across Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia.
Sanofi Global Health builds impactful partnerships around a holistic three-pillar approach: providing affordable treatments, supporting ministries of health and NGOs in strengthening local health systems, and scaling-up inclusive businesses in the private sector.
The 25m€ Sanofi Impact investment fund, announced in July 2022, aims to support the scale-up of a portfolio of impactful care delivery ventures, through financing and technical assistance, with a specific focus on non-communicable diseases. The target portfolio could include pharmacy networks that offer reliable, accessible, and affordable medicine (and beyond), community-based models that provide a full range of services from diagnosis to care monitoring in last mile areas, or risk prevention models including micro-insurance or savings offerings.
The Impact Investment Manager will be provided the unique opportunity to contribute to improving the lives of underserved populations, increasing access to health in the most vulnerable countries through the development and scale-up of innovative and inclusive healthcare models.
Main Responsibilities
The Impact Investment Manager will identify and co-develop new investment opportunities, execute transactions, and actively manage portfolio ventures of the Sanofi Global Health Impact Investment Fund.
Evaluating and developing new investment opportunities

Reviewing pipeline of ventures and shortlisting investable proposals for due diligence

Taking a proactive approach to identifying problems of performance and compliance at the fund level
Strategy and Knowledge Sharing

Actively participate in knowledge sharing and dissemination internally and externally, focusing on best practices and lessons learnt, striving for systemic change
